layer.capability: Provides immutable sparse (amplitude_power q, inverse_Lambda_power p) Decimal channel maps and generic coefficient-family product, eta derivative, Euler, average, primitive, and J_r operations without fixed channel truncation or numerical scale formation.

representation.amplitude_power: nonnegative integer q (odd q allowed for physical F = a phi)
representation.numerator_semantics: full eta derivative divided by common a(eta)^q

family_operations.product: radial convolution i+j=n with binomial eta convolution k+l=m
family_operations.J_r: zero at n=0; source(n-1,m,eta)/(n*(n+r-1)) otherwise for r=1,2
family_operations.zero_row_causality: primitive and J_r return structural zero without probing source(0,m,eta)

forbidden_promotions: forming a^q or Lambda^-p as a floating-point value
silently dropping nonzero sparse channels because of a fixed width
using a bare amplitude-power shift as a substitute for full Bell eta derivatives
identifying hand-polynomial providers with actual SchedulePressure or paper data
claiming naturalRemainder, Picard convergence, global AxisSpace certification, or paper exactness from generic algebra
layer.remaining_boundary: Instantiate the generic families with validated actual mixed-scale coefficient and Bell derivative providers, then compose the remaining Picard products, inverse operators, source-pressure path, outer inverseL/resolvent, and convergence estimates under their own provenance boundaries.
numerical_caveats: coefficient arithmetic is rounded in a local 96-digit Decimal context and is not exact real arithmetic or an interval certificate
provider compatibility, analytic eta-jet bounds, and global AxisSpace membership remain caller-side theorem obligations
the module does not evaluate amplitudes or Lambda and therefore cannot certify a numerical scale choice
